record.title: Amazon Bedrock adds Kimi K3 with cross-region availability and prompt caching
record.summary: AWS announced general availability of Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock on 18 September 2026. AWS says it is available in all AWS Regions where Bedrock is offered through cross-Region inference, and describes Kimi K3 as the first open-weight model on Bedrock with explicit prompt caching. AWS attributes to Moonshot AI the claims that Kimi K3 has 2.8 trillion parameters, native vision, a 1-million-token context window and about 2.5x better scaling efficiency than Kimi K2. The service launch is documented by AWS; model specifications and comparative efficiency remain vendor-reported, and no independent capability or cost test was conducted here.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: AWS announced Kimi K3 general availability on Amazon Bedrock on 18 September 2026 and says it can be invoked in all AWS Regions where Bedrock is available through cross-Region inference.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: AWS describes Kimi K3 as the first open-weight model on Bedrock to support explicit prompt caching; the announcement says caching can reduce latency and input costs when context is reused but provides no quantified measurement.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: AWS attributes to Moonshot AI the specifications of 2.8 trillion parameters, native vision, a 1-million-token context window and approximately 2.5x scaling-efficiency improvement over Kimi K2. These model claims were not independently verified in this review.

evidence_gaps.description: Model-card specifications, license and exact caching behavior were not inspected in this bounded review.
No independent capability, latency or cost comparison is available in this review.

brief.importance_rationale: If the service terms operate as stated, Kimi K3 availability through Bedrock makes a large open-weight model accessible within an established managed inference service and adds explicit prompt caching, which can affect deployment access and repeated-context serving costs. The commercial and operational consequence is meaningful, but the launch notice is provider documentation, Moonshot capability claims are unverified here, and no quality, latency or cost comparison was measured.
limitations: The announcement documents service availability, not independent model quality or user outcomes.
Parameter count, native vision, context length and scaling-efficiency comparison are attributed to Moonshot AI and were not independently checked here.
No pricing, cache-hit rate, latency, throughput or repeated-context cost measurement is reported in the announcement.
AWS regional availability through cross-Region inference does not establish that every customer workload or data-residency configuration is supported.
brief.summary: AWS announced general availability of Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock on 18 September 2026. AWS says it is available in all AWS Regions where Bedrock is offered through cross-Region inference, and describes Kimi K3 as the first open-weight model on Bedrock with explicit prompt caching. AWS attributes to Moonshot AI the claims that Kimi K3 has 2.8 trillion parameters, native vision, a 1-million-token context window and about 2.5x better scaling efficiency than Kimi K2. The service launch is documented by AWS; model specifications and comparative efficiency remain vendor-reported, and no independent capability or cost test was conducted here.

technical.claimed_result: The announcement does not report a new benchmark. AWS documents managed service availability and prompt-caching support; model specifications and scaling efficiency are attributed to Moonshot AI.
technical.demonstrated_result: AWS published the Bedrock launch notice and states regional availability and explicit prompt-caching support. No model capability, latency or cost result was independently measured here.
technical.mechanism: Bedrock hosts Kimi K3 with cross-Region inference. Explicit prompt caching can reuse context across calls; the announcement describes the feature but gives no workload-specific savings measurement.
technical.regime: Amazon Bedrock managed inference; AWS says availability covers all Regions where Bedrock is available through cross-Region inference. Model context, modality and parameter count are reported by AWS as Moonshot AI specifications.
technical.reproducibility: This is a service-availability announcement, not a reproducible benchmark. Independent model-card review, invocation testing and matched cost/latency measurements were not performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: No quality or cost baseline is reported in the launch notice. Kimi K2 is named only for Moonshot AI’s approximate scaling-efficiency comparison.

brief.title: Amazon Bedrock adds Kimi K3 with cross-region availability and prompt caching
brief.why_it_matters: Managed availability and prompt caching extend the deployment options for open-weight models inside a major cloud service. Whether that improves practical cost, latency or quality depends on workload and measured service terms; the announcement alone does not establish a capability advantage over other models.
